rows.name: Look-ahead bias

rows.name: Loss aversion

rows.name: Crypto wallet
rows.definition: An application or device used to view balances and manage interactions with blockchain accounts. A signing wallet uses private keys; a watch only wallet uses public information, while a custodial service controls keys for its customers.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Daily close (crypto)
rows.definition: The last price recorded before a chosen cut-off time, often 00:00 UTC. It is a charting convention, not a moment when the market actually stops.
rows.requiredAction: Definition aligns with linked approved teaching. Complete remaining claim-level external/example/note review before publication.

rows.name: Decentralised
rows.definition: Control or operation distributed among participants rather than concentrated in one central authority. The degree varies: examine who can validate, upgrade, pause or otherwise influence the system.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Decentralised finance (DeFi)
rows.definition: Financial applications that use blockchain smart contracts for activities such as swapping or lending. Some retain administrators, upgrade powers or dependencies on companies and outside data.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Decision journal
rows.definition: A dated record of each decision you make, written at the time, including your reasons, the information you had, how you felt and what you expected, with the outcome added later in a separate field.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Difficulty
rows.definition: A number showing how hard it currently is to find a valid block, compared with the easiest possible block. Higher difficulty means a lower target.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Digital signature
rows.definition: Cryptographic data that can be checked against a message and public key to verify signing with the matching private key. It does not by itself prove the rightful owner understood or willingly approved the request.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Dollar-cost averaging (DCA)
rows.definition: Investing a fixed amount at regular intervals, regardless of price. Investor.gov, the US Securities and Exchange Commission's education site, describes it as buying more when the price is low and less when it is high. In the UK it is often called pound-cost averaging.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Double-spending
rows.definition: Spending the same digital money more than once, by sending copies of it to different people. A digital cash system needs a rule for preventing conflicting spends from both becoming accepted payments under its operating assumptions.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Drawdown
rows.definition: The fall from a previous peak to a later low, written as a percentage of the peak.
rows.requiredAction: Arithmetic, stated example and calculation-scope review passed. Preserve conventions during public integration; this does not grant publication approval.

rows.name: Finfluencer
rows.definition: A social-media personality who talks about money, investing or crypto. Some are independent and careful, some are paid by the projects they mention, and many have no licence to give financial advice.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Flash loan
rows.definition: A loan designed to be borrowed and repaid, usually with a fee, within one transaction. If the required conditions fail, its state changes revert; an included failed attempt can still consume gas.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: FOMO
rows.definition: Fear of missing out: the anxious feeling that other people are gaining from something you are not part of, which pushes you to act quickly.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: FUD
rows.definition: Fear, uncertainty and doubt. In crypto discussions, the label is often used for negative claims or criticism. Check the evidence: a concern may be accurate, mistaken or deliberately misleading.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Fully diluted valuation (FDV)
rows.definition: Today's token price multiplied by the maximum supply, or by the total supply where no maximum exists. Data sites differ: CoinMarketCap uses maximum supply, while CoinGecko's guide uses total supply.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Funding rate
rows.definition: A percentage, reset at regular intervals, that decides how much one side of a perpetual futures market pays the other. It is designed to pull the perp's price towards the spot price.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Gas
rows.definition: The unit that measures how much computing effort an Ethereum operation needs. You pay for gas in ether.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Governance token
rows.definition: A token that gives its holders voting power over a protocol's rules, settings or treasury.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Gwei
rows.definition: A small unit of ether used to price gas: 1 gwei is one-billionth of an ETH (0.000000001 ETH), and 1 ETH = 1,000,000,000 gwei.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Halving
rows.definition: In Bitcoin, the scheduled reduction by half of the new block subsidy every 210,000 blocks under its issuance rules. It changes new issuance, not existing wallet balances or transaction fees.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Hash
rows.definition: A short, fixed-length code produced from any amount of data by a hash function. For the same specified function, identical data gives the same hash. A changed input will ordinarily produce a different output, although collisions are mathematically possible.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Honeypot token
rows.definition: A token whose contract lets people buy but blocks or heavily penalises selling, usually through hidden rules that only the creator can bypass.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Hot wallet
rows.definition: A wallet whose private keys are stored on an internet-connected device: convenient for regular use, but more exposed to malware and remote attacks.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Investing
rows.definition: Putting money into an asset you plan to hold for a long time, accepting that its value may fall, in the hope it is worth more later.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Issuance
rows.definition: The creation of new units of a currency. In Bitcoin, all new coins are issued through the block subsidy paid to miners.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: KYC and AML
rows.definition: KYC is the process of verifying a customer's identity. AML is the wider set of rules that require financial firms to prevent, detect and report money laundering and terrorist financing.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Layer 1
rows.definition: A base blockchain that agrees on its own blocks and secures itself, such as Bitcoin or Ethereum.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Layer 2
rows.definition: A separate network that processes transactions away from a layer 1 but relies on that layer 1 for security, for example by posting its data or proofs back to it.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Legal wrapper
rows.definition: A company, foundation or association set up under a country's law to give a DAO a legal identity and, depending on the law, limit its members' personal liability.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Liquid staking token
rows.definition: A token representing a claim on pooled staked assets under the service rules. Rewards may appear through more tokens or a changing redemption rate; trading price, redemption timing and backing can differ.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Liquidation
rows.definition: Forced reduction or closure when a trading position fails its margin requirements, or seizure of collateral when a lending position crosses its liquidation threshold. The trigger and process depend on the venue or protocol.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Loss aversion
rows.definition: The tendency for a loss to feel more painful than a gain of the same size feels good, measured from a reference point such as the purchase price.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Loss budget
rows.definition: The total amount of money, written as a cash figure in your home currency, that you have decided in advance you could lose on crypto without touching essential money or your emergency fund.
rows.requiredAction: Definition aligns with linked approved teaching. Complete remaining claim-level external/example/note review before publication.

rows.name: LP token
rows.definition: A record of a liquidity provider position and its withdrawal rights under a pool design. Some systems use fungible tokens; others use NFTs. Withdrawable assets and fee collection depend on that design.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Malware
rows.definition: Software designed to harm you or your device, for example by stealing data, watching what you type or changing what you copy, paste or see.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Market capitalisation
rows.definition: The latest price of one token multiplied by its circulating supply: a snapshot estimate, not money invested or money that could be withdrawn.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Maximalism
rows.definition: In crypto, the belief that one network or coin will, or should, replace all others. Bitcoin maximalism is the best-known form, but every large coin has its own devoted community.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Maximum supply
rows.definition: The stated upper supply limit under an asset's current rules, where such a limit exists. Check how the limit is enforced and whether anyone has power to change those rules.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Memecoin
rows.definition: A crypto-asset whose appeal comes mainly from a joke, theme or online community rather than from a product or service.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Memo or destination tag
rows.definition: An extra field, sent with a transfer on certain networks, that tells a receiving service which customer the funds belong to when many customers share one address.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Mempool
rows.definition: A node's list of valid transactions that have been broadcast but not yet included in a block.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Mining
rows.definition: Creating valid Bitcoin blocks, which requires showing proof of work. A miner is a person who runs mining machines, or the machine itself.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Multisig wallet
rows.definition: A wallet that needs signatures from a set number of separate keys (for example, two of three) before a transaction is valid.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Network (in a transfer)
rows.definition: The blockchain that carries a particular transfer. Sender and receiver must use the same one for the same token, even when the token's name and logo look identical elsewhere.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: NFT (non-fungible token)
rows.definition: A token with its own unique ID, recorded on a blockchain, that shows which address holds that particular item.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Nonce
rows.definition: A number in the block header that miners change freely. Each new nonce gives ordinarily a different hash, like printing a new ticket.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Notional value
rows.definition: A reference value describing the exposure represented by a derivatives position. For a simple linear contract, quantity times contract multiplier times the stated reference price gives notional; other contract designs use different conventions.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Off-chain governance
rows.definition: Deciding protocol changes through public proposals, discussion and voluntary software upgrades, rather than through votes recorded on the blockchain.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: On-ramp and off-ramp
rows.definition: An on-ramp converts national currency into crypto, for example by bank transfer or card. An off-ramp converts crypto back into national currency and pays it out.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Open interest (OI)
rows.definition: The number of derivatives contracts still open at a point in time. Each contract has one long side and one short side, and it is counted once.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Over-collateralised loan
rows.definition: A loan supported by collateral worth more than the borrowed amount at the stated valuation time. This buffer can shrink; liquidation, price gaps or other failures can still leave losses.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Passphrase (BIP-39)
rows.definition: Optional extra text, chosen by you, that is combined with the seed phrase to create a separate wallet. Without the exact passphrase, the seed phrase alone opens a different wallet.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Peer-to-peer
rows.definition: A system where participants deal with each other directly, instead of routing everything through one central organisation.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Permit signature
rows.definition: An off-chain signed message that, when someone submits it, creates a token approval without you sending the approval transaction yourself.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Personal circuit breaker
rows.definition: A rule you write in advance that pauses your decisions when a named trigger appears, such as a price spike, a "last chance" message or a loss.
rows.requiredAction: Definition aligns with linked approved teaching. Complete remaining claim-level external/example/note review before publication.

rows.name: Phishing
rows.definition: An attempt to trick you into revealing a secret, visiting a fake site, installing harmful software or approving a transaction, by pretending to be someone you trust.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Ponzi scheme
rows.definition: A fraud that pays "returns" to existing investors from new investors' deposits rather than from any real profit, so it must collapse once new money dries up.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Pre-commitment
rows.definition: Making a decision in advance, usually in writing, so that your future self in a heated moment has a clear rule to follow instead of deciding from scratch.
rows.requiredAction: Definition aligns with linked approved teaching. Complete remaining claim-level external/example/note review before publication.

rows.name: Proof of reserves
rows.definition: A check or report concerning selected assets controlled by a provider at a stated time. Its scope varies and may omit liabilities or other obligations; it does not by itself establish solvency.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Pseudonymity
rows.definition: Acting under a persistent identifier, such as a wallet address, that is not your name but can be linked to you if other information connects them.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Pump-and-dump
rows.definition: A scheme in which insiders buy a token cheaply, hype it to attract buyers, and sell their holdings into the rising price, leaving later buyers with losses.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Real-world asset (RWA) token
rows.definition: A token linked to an asset or economic exposure outside the blockchain, such as a bond or property. Actual ownership, redemption and enforceable rights depend on its legal structure and documents.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Rebalancing
rows.definition: Bringing a portfolio back to the mix you originally chose after price moves have shifted it. Investor.gov names three ways: selling some of what has grown too large and buying what has shrunk, buying only the smaller parts with new money, or directing new contributions to them.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Recovery plan
rows.definition: A written, offline summary of what crypto you hold, where the backups are, and the steps needed to recover access, designed so that it does not by itself reveal any secret.
rows.requiredAction: Definition aligns with linked approved teaching. Complete remaining claim-level external/example/note review before publication.

rows.name: Rehypothecation
rows.definition: Using collateral received from a customer as collateral for the recipient's own borrowing or other obligations. The agreement and applicable rules determine whether this is allowed. Lending or reusing customer assets is a broader category.
rows.requiredAction: Approved definition correction applied. Complete final whole-meaning verification, including factual examples and notes; publication remains blocked.

rows.name: Relationship investment scam ("pig butchering")
rows.definition: A fraud in which a scammer builds a friendship or romance over weeks, then persuades the victim to "invest" in crypto on a fake platform, encouraging ever larger deposits before taking everything. The slang name comes from the idea of fattening a pig before slaughter.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Rug pull
rows.definition: A scam in which a token's creators abandon the project and take the money, leaving buyers with tokens that are worth little or nothing.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Seed phrase (recovery phrase)
rows.definition: An ordered set of words used by a compatible wallet to derive recovery keys. A BIP 39 wallet may also require its exact passphrase; multisig recovery may require other keys. Treat recovery material as secret.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: SIM swap
rows.definition: A fraud in which a criminal takes control of your phone number by persuading or bribing your mobile provider to move it to a SIM card they hold.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Slashing
rows.definition: A penalty in proof of stake that destroys part of a validator's deposit when it provably breaks the rules, for example by voting for two conflicting blocks.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Slashing
rows.definition: A penalty that destroys part of a validator's staked deposit and removes it from the network, for actions that break the protocol's rules.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Smart contract
rows.definition: A blockchain program whose rules execute when called under the network conditions. It can move assets or update records, but may contain bugs or depend on administrator permissions, upgrades and external data.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Spread
rows.definition: The difference between the highest price a buyer is offering (best bid) and the lowest price a seller is asking (best ask).
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Stablecoin
rows.definition: A crypto token designed to hold a steady value against a reference, usually a national currency such as the US dollar. Stablecoins aim to hold a peg; they carry no guarantee and are not bank deposits.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Sunk-cost fallacy
rows.definition: Treating money, time or effort already spent as a reason to keep going, even though that past cost cannot be recovered by continuing.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Supply cap
rows.definition: The maximum number of units that can ever exist. For Bitcoin, the protocol rules mean no more than 21 million BTC will ever exist.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Target
rows.definition: In Bitcoin proof of work, the threshold the block header hash must be less than or equal to. A lower target makes a qualifying hash less likely per attempt.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: The DAO
rows.definition: An Ethereum smart contract investment project launched in 2016. Its June 2016 exploit prompted a disputed July hard fork; the chains continued as Ethereum and Ethereum Classic.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Token
rows.definition: A digital asset issued using an existing blockchain. Many tokens use smart contracts to maintain balances and transfer rules, but technical designs, permissions and holder rights vary.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Total supply
rows.definition: All tokens created so far, minus any that have been verifiably burned. It includes tokens that are still locked.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Total value locked (TVL)
rows.definition: The combined market value of the crypto deposited in a DeFi protocol's smart contracts at a given moment.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Trading
rows.definition: Buying and selling, or opening and closing market positions, to benefit from price changes. Holding periods vary. Costs, execution and losses matter even when the activity follows a written plan.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Transaction
rows.definition: In the Bitcoin context, a transaction spends earlier outputs and creates new outputs with specified spending conditions. These may require a signature, several signatures or other conditions. Other blockchains use different transaction models.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Travel Rule
rows.definition: A FATF standard concerning collection and secure transmission of originator and beneficiary information for relevant transfers involving regulated providers. National implementation and applicable requirements vary.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Trusted third party
rows.definition: An organisation, such as a bank or payment company, that both sides of a payment rely on to keep the record and settle disputes.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: UTXO (unspent transaction output)
rows.definition: An output that has been received but not yet spent. Your wallet's balance is the total of all the UTXOs it can spend.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Value capture
rows.definition: The share of a network's fees or other income that reaches token holders, for example through burns, buybacks or staking rewards.
rows.requiredAction: Definition aligns with linked approved teaching. Complete remaining claim-level external/example/note review before publication.

rows.name: Wallet drainer
rows.definition: A malicious website or script that persuades you to connect your wallet and sign a request which lets the attacker move your funds.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Wash trading
rows.definition: Buying and selling the same asset at nearly the same time without any real change in who owns it, usually to make trading look busier than it is.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Wash trading
rows.definition: Buying and selling the same asset, at the same time, without any real change in who owns it, to create a false picture of trading volume and demand.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Watch-only wallet
rows.definition: A wallet that tracks addresses using public information without holding their signing keys. It can display activity and, in some implementations, prepare transactions or broadcast transactions signed elsewhere. It cannot independently authorise spending from those addresses.
rows.requiredAction: Approved definition correction applied. Complete final whole-meaning verification, including factual examples and notes; publication remains blocked.

rows.name: Withdrawal allow-list
rows.definition: A setting that lets your account send crypto only to addresses you have saved in advance, often with a waiting period before a new address can be used.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Yield
rows.definition: The return you earn on crypto you deposit, lend or stake, usually shown as a yearly percentage. It is a variable estimate, not a promise.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Ether
rows.definition: The native asset of Ethereum, abbreviated ETH. It is used for transaction fees and staking under Ethereum rules. Ethereum is the network; ether is its native asset.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Private key
rows.definition: Secret cryptographic data used to create signatures for the associated account or spending condition. Someone who obtains the necessary signing keys may gain control of the assets.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Public key
rows.definition: Cryptographic data associated with a private key and used to verify its signatures. An address may be derived from keys or other spending information, depending on the network.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Proof of work
rows.definition: A mechanism requiring demonstrable computational work. In Bitcoin, miners search for a qualifying block header hash and nodes verify the block against the protocol rules.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Proof of stake
rows.definition: A consensus approach in which validators commit stake and follow rules for proposing and voting on blocks. Rewards and penalties encourage correct participation; details differ between networks.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Validator
rows.definition: A protocol participant that performs specified validation, proposal or voting duties. In Ethereum proof of stake, validators use stake and signing keys under the consensus rules.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Oracle
rows.definition: A mechanism supplying information to blockchain applications, often bringing outside data such as prices on chain. Its sources, update rules and trust assumptions affect applications that rely on it.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Decentralised exchange
rows.definition: A trading application using blockchain contracts to coordinate swaps or orders. Custody, permissions and execution designs vary; AMMs are one design rather than the definition of every DEX.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Token approval
rows.definition: Permission allowing a specified spender to transfer a defined token amount from an account, under the token rules. An allowance may be created by an on chain approval or a supported permit signature.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Slippage
rows.definition: The difference between an expected or quoted execution outcome and the outcome actually obtained. It may be favourable or adverse; compare compatible price and quantity references.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Price impact
rows.definition: The change in available price associated with the size of your own trade relative to available liquidity. A larger trade in a shallow pool can have a larger effect.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.

rows.name: Vesting
rows.definition: A schedule under which an allocation becomes available according to time or other conditions. Read who can claim it, the start, any initial waiting period and the release rules.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Token unlock
rows.definition: An event or schedule that removes restrictions on allocated tokens, making specified units available under the project terms. Availability is different from an actual sale.
rows.requiredAction: Obtain and read a primary source directly supporting this meaning and its scope.

rows.name: Loan to value
rows.definition: The debt value divided by the collateral value, usually expressed as a percentage at a stated valuation time. Protocols set borrowing limits separately from liquidation thresholds.
rows.requiredAction: Complete a claim-level check of definition, scope and any factual example or note; core evidence alone is not a complete pass.
